value.rationale: The Dürer graph is a canonical 12-vertex cubic polyhedral generalized Petersen graph, giving a naturally motivated exact edge-failure monitoring benchmark. The result is a complete classification of 400 successful sensor choices, not a small numeric increment: it derives a factorized generating polynomial, proves a pure six-vertex minimal family, and identifies a Cartesian-product graph on all 16 optimal local sensor placements. It isolates how two triangle constraints control global monitoring and relocation; no artificial parameter slice is introduced.
